prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the crowded room into near foreground people and farther background clutter: in frame 1, the seated person at lower left is roughly 0.7–1.2 m away, while the standing people behind are about 2–4 m away. In frames 2–3, a person or body surface fills most of the centre and right foreground, apparently within about 0.1–0.5 m and occluding nearly the entire room; the narrow dark gaps indicate more distant space behind. In frame 4, two people leaning forward are approximately 0.5–1.5 m ahead, with one left of centre and another upper-right, while the floor and room extend several metres behind them; in frame 5, a head and shoulder are extremely close at centre-left, a standing person is around 1–2 m ahead, and the large object at lower right is within roughly 0.5–1 m. This near/far ordering is much clearer than in the RGB, but exact metre estimates are uncertain, bright background openings appear misleadingly near, and depth boundaries around overlapping bodies, furniture, and image edges are coarse or inconsistent.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates several people in frame 1: a large partly cropped person occupies the lower-left foreground, with at least three smaller people progressively farther back around the centre-left and upper centre, making their overlap and left-to-right placement clearer than in the RGB. Frames 2–3 are dominated by a very close person mask covering much of the centre, with only a small partial person at the lower-right edge in frame 2 and no confidently segmented subject in frame 3, consistent with strong foreground occlusion. In frame 4, a bent person appears near centre-right, while frame 5 contains a large foreground person across the lower centre/right, a partly visible person at the far right edge, and another cropped figure above; these masks show who overlaps whom but do not directly provide metric distance or reliable facing direction. The map is unreliable where masks merge, truncate at frame boundaries, or disappear, and the small region labelled "cake" near a person's head in frame 5 appears inconsistent with the RGB and should not be trusted for object identity or position.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects no usable skeletons in frames 1–4, so it contributes little there about body orientation, gaze, reach, or changes in posture despite people being visible in the RGB. In frame 5 it shows one upright upper body near the right side, roughly 1–2 m in front of the camera wearer, with the torso oriented mostly toward the camera and one magenta hand extending down and to the right. That hand appears within the person's own arm's reach of the nearby foreground surface, while the skeleton does not establish that it is within the camera wearer's reach; the lower body continues downward but is partly cut off or incompletely detected. The skeleton makes limb arrangement clearer than the RGB, but the scattered head points, missing joints and people, distorted right arm/hand cluster, and lack of face landmarks make gaze direction and precise inter-person distances unreliable.
